# Psychometric method {#sec-metodo-psicometrico}



::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Status:** first draft (November 2, 2026) of chapter 5 of the manual, expanded on November 8, 2026 with the watch zone and links to [From the lab to the manual](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/avances.html) (*in Spanish*). It brings together in one place how tasks are scored, how reliability and validity are estimated, how norms are built and how to decide whether a change matters. Each section states **what is done**, **which study on the group's [research agenda](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/agenda.html) (*in Spanish*) develops it** and **what is missing**. How each task sheet is put together is described in [How each task sheet is built](metodo.en.qmd), and decisions already taken in [Methodological decisions](decisiones.en.qmd). *Translated from the Spanish version of November 27, 2026.*
:::

**In one sentence.** Each task is analyzed with the method that fits the way it measures (not all with α), each score is reported with its margin of error, and each use the manual proposes (screening, monitoring, identification) rests on specific evidence [@aera2014; @kane2013].

## Chapter map

| Section | What it answers | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 5.1 Scores | Which number represents each task and when a session is not valid | Families and main measure defined; detectors of anomalous sessions being tested |
| 5.2 Reliability | How much error each score has | 2021 α and stability for part of the tasks; error band and P20–P30 watch zone (November 8); ω and IRT pending |
| 5.3 Validity | What each score is useful for | Predictive validity against persistent difficulty; Woodcock-Muñoz external criterion; structure and invariance pending |
| 5.4 Norms | Whom a child is compared with | Empirical norms by time point and by form (November 3); first analysis of continuous norms on months of instruction in the pilot task sheets; final continuous norms pending |
| 5.5 How much change matters | When progress is real and important | Reliable change in letters and speed; regression to the mean quantified (November 8); anchors in progress |
| 5.6 Fairness | Whether the task measures the same in all groups | Differential prediction in the letters task sheet; the rest pending |

The analyses behind these sections are in the group's internal workspace (restricted access).

## 5.1 Scores

**One main measure per task, according to its family.** Tasks are grouped into seven families according to how they measure: accuracy, rapid naming, oral reading fluency, time-limited efficiency, decision with response time, span and memory, and comprehension. The family determines the main measure, its transformation and the reliability method (see [How tasks are grouped](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/agrupacion.html#sec-familias) (*in Spanish*)).

**Higher is better.** In the manual all scores are presented so that a high value is good and a low percentile indicates difficulty. Times are converted into rates (stimuli per second, words per minute).

**Understandable units.** Where possible, the score is also given in a unit a teacher understands: words per minute, minutes to read 1,000 words, or "reads like a child of…" (see [Norms by reading level](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/baremo-nivel-lector.html) (*in Spanish*)).

**Session validity.** Item-level times make it possible to detect an anomalous administration: times of zero, different units, interruptions, responses that are too fast, or results inconsistent with the same child at other time points. A first set of rules fixed in advance has been tested on the rapid naming tasks. The proposal is that each score carry a **reliable session** or **check** flag.

- **Missing:** extend the detectors to all tasks and decide the thresholds.

## 5.2 Reliability {#sec-fiabilidad}

**The method depends on the family.** Internal consistency (α, ω) only makes sense in accuracy tasks without a time limit. In speeded tasks α overestimates reliability, and test–retest or parallel forms are appropriate.

| Family | Main reliability | Complement |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy, comprehension, span | ω (or KR-20) from item responses | Test–retest; IRT and conditional standard error |
| Rapid naming, reading fluency | Test–retest and parallel forms | Reliability across cards or lists |
| Time-limited, decision | Test–retest; split-half by time | Joint model of speed and accuracy |

**What is available today.** Of the 110 assessment tasks in the catalog, 55 have a 2021 α and 33 have stability across successive administrations (ρ); 64 have at least one of the two and 46 have no reliability data yet. Stability mixes measurement error and real change, so it is a lower bound.

**Standard error and bands.** Each percentile comes with its 90% confidence band, computed with the standard error of measurement. With IRT, the error is **conditional**: wider at the extremes, where risk decisions are made.

**What a reliability of .85 implies.** A child whose true level is at P20 may appear not at risk in about 4 of every 10 assessments. The interactive simulation is in [The dancing percentile](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/avances.html#sec-baila) (*in Spanish*). That is why reports use a **watch zone between P20 and P30**, in which no label is given until the next assessment (see [The watch zone](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/avances.html#sec-vigilar) (*in Spanish*)).

- **Missing:** ω and IRT with the item-level responses of the new platform for all class A and B tasks; short-term test–retest in the speeded tasks. This is what could change the most quality classes.

## 5.3 Validity

| Source of evidence | What is done | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Content | Description of the task, items and instructions read from the platform; brief theoretical framework per task | In the pilot task sheets and in 18 frameworks by domain |
| Internal structure | Factors (precursors, decoding, fluency, comprehension) and networks by age | Exploratory networks by age; confirmatory factor analysis missing |
| Invariance | By sex, format (platform, paper, tablet), period and region | TECLE paper–platform equivalence; the rest pending |
| Convergent and external criterion | Correlation with external tests | Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (see [Validity against the Woodcock-Muñoz battery](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html) (*in Spanish*)) |
| Predictive and diagnostic | AUC, sensitivity, specificity and predictive values against persistent reading difficulty | Done with cross-cohort validation (see [How we estimate risk](riesgo.en.qmd)) |
| Consequences | False positives by group; effect of the report on decisions | Pending |

**The criterion.** Reading difficulty is defined with the child's whole trajectory from age 6 to 11, in certainty levels (persistent, transient, typical…), not with a single assessment. This makes the criterion more stable and reduces spectrum bias. When the criterion contains the task itself, the AUC is presented only as agreement, not as predictive validity.

**Beyond the cut-off.** The manual proposes giving probabilities and not only a cut-off: likelihood ratios by score band and posterior probability according to the school's prevalence. The first analyses show that a well-calibrated Bayesian model outperforms the single cut-off, and that multiplying likelihood ratios overestimates risk when indicators are correlated.

- **Missing:** confirmatory factor analysis by age, invariance by sex and format, and group agreement on the certainty levels and the threshold for severe difficulty (P10 vs. −1.5 SD).

## 5.4 Norms

**The reference sample.** Norms describe development without intervention: the reference is the children from schools that did not implement Preleo with their cohort. All equivalent cohorts are pooled, unless one departs by more than 1 SD (see [Methodological decisions](decisiones.en.qmd)).

**By time point, not only by school year.** With three assessments per school year, a single norm per school year flags almost a quarter of the children as "at risk" in the first term. That is why norms are built by school year and term, and from age 4 to 6 they are refined by age in months (see [Norms by school year or by term](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/baremos-trimestre.html) (*in Spanish*)).

**Continuous norms.** The aim is to replace the empirical tables with continuous norms by age (cNORM or GAMLSS), which smooth the percentiles, allow norming at any exact age and use all cohorts at once.

- **Missing:** continuous norms for class A tasks, separate tables for Preleo schools, and norms for age 3 and for the versions in other languages.

## 5.5 How much change matters {#sec-cambio-importa}

In a monitoring system, the key question is not only where a child stands, but **whether they have really progressed** and **whether that progress matters**. The manual answers with three complementary indicators:

1. **Reliable change index:** whether the difference between two assessments exceeds what is expected from measurement error. Already in the letters and speed task sheets.
2. **Growth percentile:** how much a child has progressed compared with those who started at the same level.
3. **Minimal important change:** how much change matters, anchored in external criteria (reading prognosis, teacher judgment, the shift from transient to persistent difficulty) [@anvari2021anclas].

**Beware of regression to the mean.** Among children flagged as at risk, some "leave" risk at the next assessment purely because of measurement error: with a reliability of .85, more than one in four without having changed (see [Leaving risk is not always improving](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/avances.html#sec-salir) (*in Spanish*)). That is why leaving risk is confirmed with another assessment.

- **Missing:** settle the anchors and apply the three indicators to the class A reading tasks.

## 5.6 Fairness

A fair task measures the same thing and makes the same errors in all groups. This is checked in two ways: **differential functioning** of items and scores (sex, school socioeconomic status, format, region) and **differential prediction**, that is, whether the same cut-off is equally accurate in all groups. The letters task sheet has already shown that, at the same score, children from low-SES schools are at greater risk; for that reason the cut-off is not adjusted for socioeconomic status.

- **Missing:** false-positive rates by group in the screening tasks.

## Reproducibility

All computations are done with R scripts on the project's computer, which read the complete data and export only aggregated tables. The book is built from those tables, and the code is in the repository. Before confirmatory studies, the analysis plan is preregistered (see [How each task sheet is built](metodo.en.qmd#reproducibilidad)).
